quote:
Thus, when plantation forestry is under consideration as part of 
FLR, the use of non-native species and species with potential to become invasive should be avoided.
retained_meaning: Avoid non-native and potentially invasive species in FLR plantation design.
intake_disposition: Species-origin/design safeguard, not a spatial invasive-cover mask; reconcile contrasting case practices explicitly.

quote:
Protecting and restoring the soil—particularly replenishing 
soil organic matter—is crucial for facilitating restoration.
retained_meaning: Replenishing soil organic matter facilitates restoration.
intake_disposition: SOM is not soil_organic_carbon; intervention recommendation not measured SOC suitability curve; no matching raw SOM variable.

quote:
The success of FLR depends on the extent and nature 
of existing environmental stresses. Sites with a strong 
seasonal climate, exposure, low soil fertility and other 
environmental stresses are likely to be more difficult to 
restore than those that have more benign conditions.
retained_meaning: Strong seasonal climate increases restoration difficulty.
intake_disposition: Broad FLR statement does not isolate forest family. No exact measured-variable mapping: do not substitute rainfall variability, wind/aspect, or SOC/CEC for source terms. Retain qualitative direction; no numeric scores.

restore than those that have more benign conditions.
retained_meaning: Low soil fertility increases restoration difficulty.

quote:
This is particularly important because experimental trials have shown that 
many native species require shelter for successful establishment.
retained_meaning: Many native species require shelter; taxon-specific needs not resolved here.
intake_disposition: Keep species-level claim; unspecified taxa/metric prevent practice-level canopy-percent mapping.

quote:
After ten years of research in mountain forests in southern Ecuador on restoration 
and reforestation, several native tree species with good growth responses (e.g. 
Handroanthus chrysanthus, Cedrela montana and Juglans neotropica) have been 
identified in open field conditions. Some species (e.g. Podocarpus oleifolius and
P. sprucei) were able to grow under the shelter provided by Pinus and Alnus trees
retained_meaning: Reported successful open-field setting for three species, sheltered growth for two; not comparative preference.
intake_disposition: Five species retained; no measured light/canopy-cover variable or individual response scale. Do not promote to practice-level canopy curve.

quote:
Both shelter tree species demonstrated potential for enrichment planting with native 
species. Thinning operations resulted in clearer effects for enrichment plantings in 
pine plantations, and the seedlings of all species showed consistently higher growth 
rates with increased thinning intensity
retained_meaning: Higher thinning intensity associated with higher seedling growth, especially pine enrichment.
intake_disposition: Silvicultural treatment response. Do not equate thinning intensity to mapped canopy cover or irradiance; full tested taxa unresolved.

quote:
Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) represent the dominant mycorrhizal form in 
tropical (native) trees, improving the nutrient uptake, water balance and pathogen 
tolerance of their host plants. However, the forestry sites used in this project for 
afforestation with native tree species potentially provide a poor AMF inoculum: 
Pinus patula only forms associations with ectomycorrhizae, whereas roots of 
Alnus acuminata are associated with ectomycorrhizae, AMF and the nitrogen-
fixing actinomycete Frankia
retained_meaning: Native-tree AMF function and potentially poor inoculum under plantation hosts.
intake_disposition: Species/soil-biota context; no canonical inoculum measure, numerical threshold or general planting exclusion.

quote:
Repeated fires originating in 
neighbouring smallholder plots and soil degradation resulting from overgrazing and 
inherent soil fragility precluded the natural regeneration of the original forest cover.
retained_meaning: Repeated fire and soil degradation jointly precluded natural regeneration at Campo Verde.
intake_disposition: Retain combined barrier; cannot allocate independent effects or infer a quantified fire regime/soil state. No new typed compound variable.

quote:
land 
classification (according to various soil types, slope classes, terrain features and 
levels of weed competition) and evaluation (based on the classification, sites were 
evaluated to optimize silvicultural regimes in terms of soil preparation, weed 
management, soil nutrition and species choice)
retained_meaning: Actual use of soil types, slope classes, terrain features and weed competition in site classification/evaluation for silvicultural regimes.
intake_disposition: Source-specific planning use retained, direction unknown; no class boundaries/weights. Mixed production plantation and restoration scope needs family-specific source detail, not automatic active_planting assignment.

quote:
Depending 
on the landscape context, when there are nearby sources of seeds and other 
propagules, natural regeneration potential may be high, and recruited seedlings 
can occupy the space left by the harvest of Eucalyptus.
retained_meaning: Nearby seeds/propagules can support regeneration after Eucalyptus harvest.
intake_disposition: Conditional plantation-conversion setting; seeds need not come from mapped forest. Retain source proximity without substituting distance_to_forest or moving evidence into generic passive restoration.

quote:
Intensive silvopastoral systems. Implemented between 0 and 2000 m above sea 
level, intensive SPS involves more than 5000 fodder shrubs per ha and up to 500 
trees per ha. The most common shrub species are Leucaena leucocephala, Tithonia 
diversifolia and Guazuma ulmifolia, combined with fruit trees, timber trees and palms. 
Above 2000 m, intensive SPS uses 100 native trees per ha, interspersed with 2000 
forage shrubs planted in strips of four rows every 40 m.
retained_meaning: Two altitude-stratified silvopastoral designs:0–2000m and above2000m.
intake_disposition: Agroforestry cross-NbS follow-up; not forest/mangrove T4. Design classes are not a universal elevation exclusion or response score.

quote: Severe soil degradation made successful planting difficult
practice_context: Community mangrove restoration, Pyindaye Reserved Forest, Myanmar; case includes abandoned-paddy planting and degraded-forest enrichment
variable_use: Observed establishment difficulty reported as a project challenge; not a suitability calculation.
direction: Adverse effect of severe existing degradation on planting success. No measured monotonic severity-response function established.
calibration: No soil metric, severity scale, threshold, response score or weight.
mapping_hold: Observed soil degradation state cannot be replaced by soil_degradation_risk or soil_degradation_sensitivity. No ontology change made.
scope_hold: Source associates challenge with the project; does not locate it specifically to paddy planting versus enrichment or identify which soil property was responsible.
source_lineage: Case cites FREDA & ACTMANG (2012), Springate-Baginski et al. (2011), Webb et al. (2014); individual primary attribution not resolved.
review_status: unapproved source-value inventory only; not ingested EV
next_action: Resolve observed-state ontology and practice applicability; inspect cited primary evidence before any typed intake. Retain qualitative direction even if calibration remains absent.
